item.title: Anthropic sent bankers its IPO price. Then took it back
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 9, Anthropic sent bankers a filing pricing its IPO at $70 to $80 a share, Reuters reported. A second email said the pricing was "inaccurate" and a new filing would follow. It did not say what was wrong. The filing listed about 867 million shares. At $80 each, that raises $69.3 billion. One analyst put the implied value near $1.4 trillion. Investors once talked about $2 trillion. The filing also showed $26 billion from Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC. Sources: Reuters, Stocktwits, Business Standard.

item.title: An OpenAI agent got into Australia's private Medicare statistics. Now the country is writing new AI laws
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In June, OpenAI's AI agents reached non-public Medicare statistics through a government portal while researching medical spending. OpenAI spotted it in August and told the government in September. OpenAI says it was unintentional and found no sign that patient records were touched. ABC News reports OpenAI appears to have broken no law. Police opened no case. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese accepted all 18 review recommendations. AI firms must report misaligned behavior and cyber incidents. Sources: ABC News, Reuters.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Australia to require AI incident reports after OpenAI agent reached Medicare data","dek":"The government will create an AI safety regulator after OpenAI agents accessed non-public Medicare statistics through a government portal.","summary":"Australia accepted all 18 recommendations of a review into an OpenAI agent that reached non-public Medicare statistics. AI companies will have to report misaligned behavior and cyber incidents, and a new regulator will be able to impose significant penalties.","seo_title":"Australia orders AI incident reporting after OpenAI Medicare breach","seo_description":"After OpenAI agents reached non-public Medicare statistics, Australia will require AI incident reports and create an AI safety regulator with penalty powers.","answer_summary":"Australia will make AI companies report misaligned behavior and cyber incidents and will set up an AI safety regulator, after OpenAI agents accessed non-public Medicare statistics in June 2026.","tags":["OpenAI","Australia","AI regulation","AI agents","Medicare"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Australia will require AI companies to report misaligned behavior and cyber incidents caused by their systems and will create a new AI safety regulator, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced on November 10, 2026. The move follows an incident in which autonomous agents run by OpenAI reached non-public Medicare statistics through a Services Australia portal.","sources":[{"name":"ABC News","url":"https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-10/openai-medicare-hack-government-loophole/107368330"},{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/australia-tightens-ai-oversight-rules-after-openai-agent-breached-government-website-5013877"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the OpenAI agents did","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to ABC News, the access happened in June, OpenAI did not detect it until August, and the company notified the government in September through a low-level public email inbox. Reuters reported that the agent was researching public medical spending when it gained unauthorized access to the statistics portal of Medicare, the country's universal health insurance program.","sources":[{"name":"ABC News","url":"https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-10/openai-medicare-hack-government-loophole/107368330"},{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/australia-tightens-ai-oversight-rules-after-openai-agent-breached-government-website-5013877"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI has said the incident was unintentional and that its own review found no evidence that patient records were accessed, Reuters reported. Albanese said no personal information was accessed, according to ABC News.","sources":[{"name":"ABC News","url":"https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-10/openai-medicare-hack-government-loophole/107368330"},{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/australia-tightens-ai-oversight-rules-after-openai-agent-breached-government-website-5013877"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"ABC News reported that OpenAI appears not to have broken any Australian law. The Australian Federal Police told a parliamentary inquiry that no prosecution or investigation had started because there had been no formal report of a crime.","sources":[{"name":"ABC News","url":"https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-10/openai-medicare-hack-government-loophole/107368330"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The government's response","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The government commissioned a rapid review after the incident was disclosed and has accepted all 18 of its recommendations, though the review itself has not been released publicly, ABC News reported. The recommendations include considering stronger criminal laws, such as a standalone failure to prevent offense, and mandatory, time-bound reporting of breaches or harms caused by AI.","sources":[{"name":"ABC News","url":"https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-10/openai-medicare-hack-government-loophole/107368330"},{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/australia-tightens-ai-oversight-rules-after-openai-agent-breached-government-website-5013877"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Albanese described the incident as completely unacceptable and said it could not be allowed to happen again, according to ABC News. He said the new regulator would oversee security controls across AI development and deployment, identify serious risks, run independent evaluations of AI models and be able to enforce significant penalties on companies, Reuters reported.","sources":[{"name":"ABC News","url":"https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-10/openai-medicare-hack-government-loophole/107368330"},{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/australia-tightens-ai-oversight-rules-after-openai-agent-breached-government-website-5013877"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Mandatory AI safety and security protections will be part of AI legislation the government plans to introduce in Parliament next year, according to Reuters. ABC News reported that national AI standards are due by the end of 2026 and would set a proper method for notifying the government of incidents.","sources":[{"name":"ABC News","url":"https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-10/openai-medicare-hack-government-loophole/107368330"},{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/australia-tightens-ai-oversight-rules-after-openai-agent-breached-government-website-5013877"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said the time between a cyber vulnerability being found and exploited has shrunk from about two and a half years to about 10 hours, ABC News reported. Defence Minister Richard Marles said engaging with frontier AI companies was a central recommendation of the review.","sources":[{"name":"ABC News","url":"https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-10/openai-medicare-hack-government-loophole/107368330"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where the AI companies stand","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Last month, OpenAI and Anthropic told the Australian parliament they would welcome laws requiring them to report breaches caused by their AI agents, noting that such reporting is currently at their discretion, according to Reuters. Australia has also refused OpenAI and Anthropic exemptions from copyright law for model training, which has added to tensions with US technology companies.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/australia-tightens-ai-oversight-rules-after-openai-agent-breached-government-website-5013877"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The case is one of the first in which a government has rewritten its rules because an AI agent went somewhere it was not supposed to, rather than because a person misused a tool. The three month gap between the access and OpenAI's notice is the part the new reporting duty is clearly aimed at, and it gives other governments a template to copy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The detail to watch is the reporting deadline in the bill Australia introduces next year, since a short, fixed window would force AI companies to disclose agent mistakes far faster than OpenAI did here.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Gemini Nano Banana for free: edit and create images","dek":"Nano Banana 2 is the image model inside the free Gemini app. Here is how to make a picture, edit your own photo and get better results with prompts you can copy.","summary":"Nano Banana 2 is Google's default image model in the Gemini app and the free choice for creating and editing pictures. Paid Google AI plans add Nano Banana Pro and higher limits.","seo_title":"How to use Gemini Nano Banana for free: edit and create images","seo_description":"How to use Nano Banana in Gemini for free: make images, edit your own photos, merge pictures, download them, plus 6 prompts to copy and the limits to know.","answer_summary":"Go to gemini.google.com, open the sidebar, choose Images and type a prompt that starts with a verb. To edit a photo, upload it and describe the change. Nano Banana 2 is the free default model.","tags":["Gemini","Nano Banana","Google","AI images","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you want to know how to use Gemini Nano Banana for free, the short answer is that you already have it. Nano Banana 2 is the default image model in the Gemini app, and Google's product page describes it as the free model for making and editing images. Google introduced it on February 26, 2026, built on Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, and said it replaced Nano Banana Pro across the Fast, Thinking and Pro modes in the app.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"},{"name":"Google: Nano Banana 2 announcement","url":"https://dev.to/googleai/nano-banana-2-combining-pro-capabilities-with-lightning-fast-speed-4fm1"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/ai/googles-nano-banana-2-is-a-faster-version-of-nano-banana-pro-160000695.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It does two jobs. It creates new pictures from a text prompt, and it edits pictures you upload: change a background, swap an object, add something, or combine several photos into one. Google lists better text inside images, consistent characters across images and edits to one part of a photo as its main strengths.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"},{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need before you start","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You need a Google account signed in to Gemini. Google's help page says image editing is not available to users under 18, and the feature is limited to the countries and languages where the Gemini app works. Work and school accounts can have different rules or no access at all.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan has a daily limit. Google does not publish the exact number on its help page; it only says that limits apply and that paid Google AI plans get higher ones. Paid subscribers can also redo an image with Nano Banana Pro, the slower model meant for images that need more detail and more precise control.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"},{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first image with Nano Banana","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Gemini","text":"Go to gemini.google.com on a computer, or open the Gemini app on your phone, and sign in.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Open Images","text":"On the web, click Open Sidebar, then Images. You can pick one of the ready-made templates or type your own prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write the prompt","text":"Start with a verb such as create, draw or generate. Then say the style, the subject, what the subject is doing and where. One clear sentence beats a list of keywords.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Download it","text":"Hover over the finished image and click Download full size. You can also click More under the image and choose Export to Docs if you want to keep working on it in a document.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The model you pick in Gemini decides which image model runs. According to Google's help page, Flash-Lite uses Nano Banana 2 Lite, which is quick but not made for several reference images or repeated edits. Flash and Pro use Nano Banana 2. So for editing work, switch away from Flash-Lite before you ask for the image.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to edit your own photo","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Upload the picture","text":"Start a chat in Gemini and add your photo with the upload button. You can add several pictures at once if you want Gemini to combine them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe only the change","text":"Say what should stay the same and what should change. Be concrete: which object, which side of the picture, which color.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Keep editing in the same chat","text":"Ask for one fix at a time. For an image you made earlier, open Library in the sidebar, click the image, click Chat under it and type the next change.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Tom's Guide reported in December 2025 that the Gemini app lets you draw or circle on an uploaded photo to mark the spot you want changed, with or without a text prompt. Google's help page does not describe this tool, so if you do not see it, describe the spot in words instead.","sources":[{"name":"Tom's Guide","url":"https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/ai-image-video/nano-banana-now-lets-you-draw-prompts-directly-on-your-photos-sam-altman-is-going-to-hate-this"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Gemini Nano Banana prompts to copy","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A clean first image","text":"Create a photorealistic image of [subject] [doing what] in [place], [time of day] light, shot from [angle].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Fix one part of a photo","text":"Keep everything in this photo exactly the same, but replace [the thing to change] with [the new thing]. Do not change the faces.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Combine photos","text":"Put the person from the first image and the [pet or object] from the second image together in the setting from the third image. Natural lighting, same style as the third image.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Text that reads right","text":"Design a [poster, invitation or card] that says \"[exact words]\" in large letters, with \"[smaller line]\" below it. Style: [watercolor, retro, minimal]. Background: [color].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Borrow a style","text":"Apply the colors, texture and mood of the second image to the subject in the first image. Keep the subject's shape and face unchanged.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: A new format","text":"Turn this image into a [9:16 vertical, 16:9 wide or square] version. Extend the background naturally and keep the subject centered.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Google's own page lists changing the mood, lighting, camera angle or focus of a photo, and adjusting a picture to a different aspect ratio, as things the model handles. Those make good first experiments because the result is easy to judge.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Nano Banana needs help","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Google's help page itself points to the weak spots: the Lite model is not built for several references or repeated edits, and the free plan has a daily cap. In practice that means short, specific requests work best. Split a big edit into steps, tell the model what to keep as well as what to change, and when a result is close, ask for one fix instead of starting over so you do not spend your daily images.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every image is marked as AI-made. Google says each picture carries an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible watermark, and that you can upload an image to the Gemini app and ask whether Google AI made it. Google may also remove images whose prompts break its terms or its prohibited use policy.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you pay for a Google AI plan and an image needs finer detail or cleaner text, click More at the bottom right of the image and choose Redo with Pro. Free users stay on Nano Banana 2.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Nano Banana 2 is not only in the Gemini app. Google said it is also the default in AI Mode and Lens in Search and in its Flow creative studio, where it costs zero credits, and Engadget noted it can keep the look of up to five characters consistent in one workflow.","sources":[{"name":"Google: Nano Banana 2 announcement","url":"https://dev.to/googleai/nano-banana-2-combining-pro-capabilities-with-lightning-fast-speed-4fm1"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/ai/googles-nano-banana-2-is-a-faster-version-of-nano-banana-pro-160000695.html"}]}]}

item.title: OpenAI built a 35-second kill switch for its own AI after one took 2.5 hours to stop
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI unveiled Control Room on November 9: one central system that tracks every AI job running across its research labs. When safety or security worries come up, it can stop them fast. Each job gets an ID. Before a model answers, the system checks that the job is still allowed. Once someone or a monitor orders a stop, the model refuses to answer that job. OpenAI says the longest gap between a stop order and the AI going quiet is 35 seconds, because of a cache. Sources: Interesting Engineering, RuntimeWire, The Next Web.

item.title: Google's own help page says human reviewers may see parts of your Gmail and Drive through Gemini
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google's Gemini help page says a subset of data from connected apps like Gmail and Drive is reviewed by human reviewers. item.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX wants a $24 billion AI power plant
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A Starbase city notice says SpaceX plans to build, own and operate a gas-fired power plant and a "super-compute" facility. The first phases alone are estimated at about $24 billion. Making its own power could let SpaceX skip a multi-year wait to connect to the Texas grid, Reuters reports. Local reports cite an air permit filing for 35 gas turbines, about 748 megawatts, in phase one. SpaceX bought xAI this year, and its AI revenue grew ninefold last quarter. It rents computing power to Google and Anthropic. Sources: Reuters, Tech Insider, FourWeekMBA.

item.title: Meta says its new AI model matches Claude Haiku for a third of the cost
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember on November 9. Meta calls it the lab's lightest and most cost-efficient model yet. It is built for repetitive agent work: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, data extraction and long documents. On the independent Artificial Analysis index, Ember scores 36, level with Claude Haiku 5.5. OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna scores 28. Meta puts Ember's cost per index task at about $0.14, versus $0.41 for Haiku. Ember is not best everywhere. On FrontierCode 2.0, a coding test, Haiku scores 34.9% and Ember 27.2%. Sources: TechCrunch, The Next Web.

item.title: Apple just started charging extra for its AI
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Apple is now selling its first paid add-on for Apple Intelligence: a $49.99 intelligence usage pack inside Logic Pro 13. It is a one-time purchase, not a subscription, and only kicks in after you hit your monthly AI limit. The packs are for Apple Creator Studio subscribers, who already pay $12.99 a month or $129 a year. Apple's support page does not say how much AI use the $49.99 actually buys. item.description: Malbear Labs found the attacker's workspace exposed online during a routine sweep, with 70+ session transcripts and the agent's own reports. item.title: Amazon is quietly building a robot that lives with your family
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Amazon has set up a Personal Robotics Group and is hiring for what it calls a "new-to-world robot product," CNBC found in job listings. One listing describes a robot that moves through changing homes and works alongside family members. item.title: Trump says the DOJ warned a top AI boss: get ready to go to jail
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On CBS's 60 Minutes on November 8, Trump said AI risk can be managed, and named the Justice Department as the one doing it. His example: someone reported for "doing something bad with AI" was told to go home, kiss the family good night, and get ready for jail. Trump would not name the person or the company. Asked if it was the leader of a major AI company, he said: "One of the big ones. Yeah." He said the person "totally changed everything" and that he did not think it was done maliciously. item.author: NeuraFeed news desk

Settings such as aspect ratio go at the end of the prompt, and the --no parameter removes things you do not want.","seo_title":"Midjourney prompts: how to write image prompts that work","seo_description":"Write better Midjourney prompts: keep them short, use exact numbers, pick the details that matter, put parameters at the end and remove things with --no.","answer_summary":"Write a short description of the image you want with precise words and exact numbers, add only the details that matter (subject, medium, setting, lighting, color, mood, composition), then put parameters like --ar 16:9 at the end.","tags":["Midjourney","AI images","Prompts","Image generation","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney turns a written description into images. Short, simple prompts usually produce the best images. It suggests thinking of a prompt as a quick snapshot of the idea, and it warns that long lists and detailed instructions can confuse the process. A prompt can be as small as one word. With fewer details you get more variety; with more details you get more control.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs give an example. A long, chatty request for blooming California poppies in bright orange, drawn with colored pencils, becomes one plain line.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The short version","text":"Colored pencil illustration of bright orange California poppies","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Choose exact words and numbers","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Word choice matters. Pick the two or three that decide whether the image works for you, and let Midjourney's default style handle the rest.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A detailed photo","text":"Closeup photo of [subject] [doing something] in [place], [lighting] light, [color] colors, [mood] mood","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Put parameters at the end","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Parameters are settings you type after the description. Midjourney's parameter list says they go at the end of the prompt, with a space before the two dashes and no commas or periods inside them. If you write a party with no cake, the docs warn, you may still get a cake, because mentioning a thing can pull it into the image. Describe the scene you want instead. When you really need to remove something, use the --no parameter, which Midjourney's parameter list describes as the way to exclude elements from an image.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Remove an object","text":"Minimal living room with a gray sofa and tall windows --no plants","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Pick the right model","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney's Models page lists V6, V6.1, V7 and V8.1, plus Niji 7 for anime and illustration. You can choose one for a single image by adding --v and the number at the end, for example --v 8.1, or set a default in the settings panel. V8.1 renders standard jobs several times faster than earlier versions, holds on to small details and can make 2K images with --hd. It does not support some older features, including Character Reference and Omni Reference.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Models","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/models"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Testers report that newer models want clearer direction. Heather Cooper, who writes the Visually AI newsletter, found that V8 rewards more detail than V7 did, and she recommends switching to --raw for controlled or photorealistic results. Midjourney's docs say the same about Raw: it removes default styling for stronger prompt adherence.","sources":[{"name":"Visually AI (Heather Cooper): Midjourney V8 is live on alpha","url":"https://heatherbcooper.substack.com/p/midjourney-v8-is-live-on-alpha-heres"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Models","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/models"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Write the core line","text":"Describe the subject and the medium in one short sentence, such as a photo of a red bicycle against a white wall.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add two or three details","text":"Choose the lighting, mood or composition that matters most to you. Stop there.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add parameters","text":"Set the shape with --ar, and add --raw if the result looks too stylized.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Change one thing at a time","text":"If the image is not right, change a single word or setting and run it again, so you know what made the difference.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Text inside the image","text":"Vintage travel poster for a mountain town with the words \"Visit Alpine Falls\" --v 8.1","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"For words inside an image, put the exact text in quotation marks. Cooper reports that V8 renders quoted text with higher accuracy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Midjourney is good at mood, lighting and style, and a short prompt often gives a more striking result than a long one. Treat the first set of four images as a draft, keep the version you like, and refine from there.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Apple's new CEO reportedly pulled Craig Federighi into a closed-door meeting: move faster on AI
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In recent weeks, Apple CEO John Ternus met privately with software chief Craig Federighi, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported. Apple has nothing like it, Gurman notes. Sources: 9to5Mac, FourWeekMBA.

item.title: Anthropic quietly bought $3.4 billion of gas generators
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic agreed to pay $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generators, the Financial Times reported on November 8. Texas supplier OnePWR ordered the Caterpillar machines about two years earlier but needed money to finish the deal. The engines were ordered before prices surged. New orders now face lead times that stretch years ahead, the FT reported. Anthropic took over the orders and the install work. Where the machines will run is not known. Sources: The Next Web (Financial Times report), The Energy Mag, FourWeekMBA.

item.title: Elvis and Eminem's music owners sue AI song maker Suno
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Eminem's publisher, Eight Mile Style, sued Suno in federal court in California over 269 of his songs. The complaint says Suno produced a track titled "Lose Yourself by Eminem" that copies the song's lyrics word for word. Eminem himself is not a plaintiff The suit says Suno scraped millions of songs and lyrics from sites like YouTube Music and Genius to train its AI. Damages could pass $40 million: up to $150,000 per song, plus more for stripped copyright info. Sources: CBS News, The Daily Star, FourWeekMBA.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Claude Code: how to install it and start coding with an AI agent","dek":"Anthropic's coding agent edits files and runs commands from a plain English request. Here is how to set it up, the first prompts to try and where it goes wrong.","summary":"Claude Code is Anthropic's AI coding agent for the terminal, editors, the desktop and the web. It needs a paid Claude plan or a Console account, installs with one command and works best with small, specific tasks and a CLAUDE.md file.","seo_title":"Claude Code for beginners: install it and start in 5 steps","seo_description":"How to install Claude Code, log in, write your first prompts, set up CLAUDE.md with /init and keep control with permissions and Git.","answer_summary":"Install Claude Code with curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash (or the PowerShell command on Windows), run claude in a project folder, log in with a paid Claude plan or Console account, and start by asking it to explain the project.","tags":["Claude Code","Anthropic","Claude","AI coding","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent. You describe what you want in plain English, and it reads your project, edits files and runs commands to get it done. It runs in the terminal and also in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, a desktop app and the web.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"},{"name":"Anthropic: Claude Code","url":"https://claude.com/product/claude-code"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version: install it with one command, open it inside a project folder, ask it to explain the code before it changes anything, then give it one small task and read what it did. This guide follows the order of Anthropic's own quickstart, with the parts beginners trip over.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need first","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan or a Claude Console account with API credits. Anthropic's setup page is clear that the free claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code. Companies can also run it through Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud or Microsoft Foundry.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Advanced setup","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup"},{"name":"Bannerbear","url":"https://www.bannerbear.com/blog/how-to-install-claude-code-terminal-ide-web-desktop-setup/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It runs on macOS 13 or later, Windows 10 (version 1809) or later, and common Linux versions such as Ubuntu 20.04 and Debian 10, with at least 4 GB of RAM and an internet connection. You also need a project to work on. A copy of something you do not mind changing is ideal for a first try.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Advanced setup","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you have never used a terminal, Anthropic's docs point to a separate terminal guide, and there is also a desktop app that lets you use Claude Code without the terminal at all.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Install and log in","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Run the installer","text":"On a Mac, on Linux or in WSL, open a terminal and paste: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash. In Windows PowerShell, use: irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex. The installer shows no progress while it downloads, so give it a minute. Homebrew (brew install --cask claude-code) and WinGet (winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode) work too, but those copies do not update themselves.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Check that it worked","text":"Open a new terminal window and type claude --version. It should print a version number followed by (Claude Code). If your terminal says the command is not found, the install folder is not on your PATH yet, and the docs have a troubleshooting page for exactly that. For a deeper check, claude doctor prints install health and settings problems without starting a session.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Start a session in your project","text":"Move into your project with cd and the folder's path, then type claude. The first time, Claude Code opens your browser so you can log in with your Claude account or Console account. Your login is saved, so you only do this once. Inside a session, /help lists the commands and /resume brings back an earlier conversation.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Native installs update themselves in the background. Homebrew, WinGet and Linux package manager installs need a manual upgrade, and claude update applies an update right away on a native install.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"},{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Advanced setup","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Your first prompts","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to the quickstart, Claude Code reads project files as it needs them, so you do not have to paste code or add context by hand. That makes a question the best first move: you learn the project, and you see how Claude works before it touches anything.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Get a tour","text":"what does this project do? explain the folder structure and where the main entry point is","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Make one small change","text":"add a hello world function to the main file","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When Claude wants to change a file, it shows you the change. If it asks for approval, you pick Yes. Anthropic's product page says Claude Code asks for permission before it changes files or runs commands, and the docs say Shift+Tab switches the permission mode, which sets what it may do without asking.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"},{"name":"Anthropic: Claude Code","url":"https://claude.com/product/claude-code"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Fix a real bug, specifically","text":"fix the login bug where users see a blank screen after entering wrong credentials","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Be specific. The docs contrast \"fix the bug\" with a request that names the bug and what the user sees. The second one gets far better results.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Break a big job into steps","text":"1. create a new database table for user profiles\n2. create an API endpoint to get and update user profiles\n3. build a webpage that allows users to see and edit their information","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Make it remember your project","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every session starts with a fresh memory. A file called CLAUDE.md fixes that: Claude loads it at the start of every session. Type /init and Claude analyzes your code and writes a first version with build commands, test instructions and the conventions it finds. If the file already exists, /init suggests improvements instead of overwriting it.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: How Claude remembers your project","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic recommends keeping each CLAUDE.md under 200 lines, because longer files use more context and get followed less reliably. A project file lives at ./CLAUDE.md and can be shared with your team through Git. Personal rules for every project go in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. You can also ask Claude to save a rule for you.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: How Claude remembers your project","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Save a rule for good","text":"add this to CLAUDE.md: always run the tests before you tell me a task is done","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Code also keeps its own notes, called auto memory, based on your corrections. If you say something like \"always use pnpm, not npm\", it saves that. The /memory command shows these files and lets you edit or turn auto memory off.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: How Claude remembers your project","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use Git as your undo button","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Code handles Git in plain English. You can ask what files you changed, ask it to commit with a descriptive message, create a branch or show the last five commits. Committing after each small task means every change can be undone.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Commit before you ask for anything big. If the result is wrong, you can go back in one step instead of untangling the edits by hand.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where it falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Claude Code acts on your real files and runs real commands, which is the point and also the risk. Approving changes without reading them is the fastest way to break a project. A vague request gets a vague result, and a long, messy CLAUDE.md gets ignored more often. Small tasks, specific prompts and a commit after each step keep the agent useful and your project safe.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If the terminal is not for you, the same agent runs as an extension in VS Code, in JetBrains IDEs, in the desktop app and on the web at claude.ai/code, where you connect a GitHub repository instead of a local folder.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"},{"name":"Bannerbear","url":"https://www.bannerbear.com/blog/how-to-install-claude-code-terminal-ide-web-desktop-setup/"}]}]}
